cases.prompt: A laboratory records the same experiment on several days. Each record contains the input, model revision, runtime version, device type, numerical precision, output, and validation result. Some experiments change a kernel, some change batching, and some change memory layout. A reliable comparison controls every unrelated variable. When an experiment is interrupted, the missing results cannot be treated as successful. Failed trials are retained because they can explain which assumptions were wrong. The team separates correctness tests from service benchmarks and measures latency only after checking output quality. Explain how these practices help:
cases.continuation: They make each comparison reproducible, preserve the evidence needed to identify regressions, and prevent incomplete experiments from being reported as successful optimizations.
